newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends at 3-month lows, awaits GCA data.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends at 3-month lows, awaits GCA data.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures ended down on Tuesday, as speculative selling drove prices to more than three-month lows, dealers said.

They added, however, that turnover was unimpressive and prices were confined to a relatively narrow range as many market participants awaited key Green Coffee Association of New York stock data due after today's close.

Benchmark September contract fell 4.15 cents a lb on the day, to 157.85 cents -- its lowest settlement since April 8 -- after ranging between 159.50 and 156.25 cents. Spot July, which expires on Monday, ended 2.50 cents lower, at 184.50 cents, while the outer months closed down 0.05 to 3.60 cents.
The July/September switch widened to 26.65 cents compared with 25.00 cents at the close on Monday, while the September/December switch narrowed to 11.95 cents from 12.50 cents.

New York coffee prices headed lower from the opening bell, as a fund-led sell-off in London overnight set a bearish tone. LIFFE September robusta coffee futures fell $150 -- or nearly 10 percent -- to close at $1,585 on Tuesday.

In New York, the active September contract slipped to a low of 156.25 cents, down 5.75 cents, but traders said roaster buying in the back months prevented further losses and held the benchmark September contract above key chart support at 155.00 cents per lb.
Some traders said the New York market may have seen some anticipatory selling ahead the Green Coffee Association of New York's monthly stock report.

Most traders expect the data, due this afternoon at 1500 EDT, to show little change in inventories during June, with most estimates coming in at plus or minus 100,000 bags. Some traders said, however, U.S. stockpiles could increase by as much as 200,000 bags.
Traders said the recent build in exchange-certified coffee stocks and mild weather in top-producer Brazil continued to dampen sentiment.
"It was actually dull today," said one broker. "But I think the market is still reflecting higher exchange stocks and good weather in Brazil."

CSCE reported after Monday's close that certified coffee inventories rose for the seventh day in a row, increasing by 1,644 60-kg bags as of July 11, to 72,245 bags. An additional 19,324 bags were pending grading, the exchange said.
Technically, traders said that after 155.00 cents, September faced support at 150.00 cents. Near-term resistance was seen at 160.00 cents.
Volume reached an estimated 6,101 lots, traders said.
